where: Section 1, last paragraph, and Exam trap 3
problem: The chapter says 'Swinging the upper part through 180° about the vertical axis is a different action: it changes face', and Exam trap 3 repeats that changing face is just swinging the upper part. This contradicts the standard definition. Changing face is the two-step operation: transit the telescope about the horizontal axis, then swing the upper plate 180° so the same target is sighted again with the vertical circle on the other side. A swing on its own only sends the telescope to a different direction; it does not put the observer on the other face of the same target.
fix: Section 1: 'Transiting is turning the telescope end for end about the horizontal axis, through 180°. Changing face means transiting and then swinging the upper part 180° about the vertical axis until the same target is sighted again; the vertical circle is now on the other side of the observer. A swing alone does not change face.' Exam trap 3: 'Confusing transiting with changing face. Transiting turns the telescope end for end about the horizontal axis; changing face is transiting plus swinging the upper part 180° to re-sight the target on the other face.'

problem: The 'what it checks' entry is 'Vertical hair lies in the plane of the line of collimation'. The vertical hair always lies in that plane by definition, so the entry does not say what the test is for. The adjustment is to make the vertical hair truly vertical, that is, perpendicular to the horizontal axis, so that raising or lowering the telescope makes a fixed point stay on the hair.
fix: 'Vertical hair truly vertical (perpendicular to the horizontal axis)'.

problem: 'The screw slides the objective to focus' is only true of external-focusing telescopes. Most instruments a student will meet are internal-focusing, where the objective is fixed and the screw moves a small focusing lens inside the tube.
fix: 'Magnifies the target; the screw moves the objective (external focus) or an internal focusing lens so the image falls on the cross hairs.'

problem: Two foot screws are turned 'towards each other'. The direction depends on where the bubble is: the thumbs go towards each other or away from each other, whichever walks the bubble to the centre. A student with the bubble at the far end of the tube will turn the wrong way by following the text literally.
fix: 'Centre the plate level bubble with two foot screws, turning both thumbs towards each other or both away from each other, choosing the direction that moves the bubble to the centre.'

problem: 'Adjustment is nothing but restoring three right angles' sets up only three conditions, but Section 4 lists six adjustments. Two of the extra three are not right-angle conditions: the altitude (telescope) level must be parallel to the line of collimation, and the vertical-circle index must read zero on a horizontal sight.
fix: 'Adjustment means restoring three right angles and two settings that go with them: the line of collimation square to the horizontal axis, the horizontal axis square to the vertical axis, and the plate level axis square to the vertical axis, with the altitude level parallel to the line of collimation and the vertical-circle index at zero.'
